summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of kidney transplant, and multiple comorbidities was admitted due to persistent low-grade fevers and hyperglycemia while on outpatient antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. Initial evaluation showed no dysuria or urinary symptoms, and urinalysis was negative for infection. She developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea and abdominal cramping, leading to temporary discontinuation of furosemide. Blood and urine cultures remained negative, and she improved clinically with a switch to a higher dose of cefpodoxime after one dose of IV ceftriaxone. Her kidney function remained stable, and immunosuppressive medications were continued. Anemia was detected, and iron studies were pending at discharge. She was discharged home in stable, afebrile condition with instructions to follow up on anemia and to avoid restarting furosemide until cleared by her provider.
